Owner, 2026-09-20: 'there needs to be a new repo (staged here as a new top-level dir -> repo later) which is an instance of fa-core, and is for the who-iris cataloge and this is an example artefact (the style guide is part of the library itself)', and later 'in future who-iris iwll be own repo. will have specialized tools/themes.' The `library` entry landed with the git mv (bean frs5), in the same change, exactly as the previous version of this comment said it would: until then its ABSENCE was load-bearing, because `resolveLibraryRef` reported `no-library-graph` for a citation naming this instance -- a different and more useful answer than 'that section is missing'. Both of those are now real answers rather than one standing in for the other. THE STYLE GUIDE IS NOW A SUBGRAPH OF THIS INSTANCE, not an instance of its own: owner, 2026-09-30, 'who voices style guide is derivative KG content from who-iris, merge content into subgraph. including docs.' The three house voices moved to `skills/voices/`, the WHO glossary to `glossary/`, and the style guide's README to `docs/style-guide.md`, all by git mv (bean qsx4). The cross-instance citation bean z7ev built for them is no longer needed by them: a voice and the publication it is read from are in one instance, so every citation is the bare, same-instance form.

assets.title: AGENTS.md — who-iris
assets.description: Cold start for work in this layer. The gap between twelve modelled nodes and a million upstream files is the POINT rather than a backlog, so it is never work to be done; every node declares its state with no default, because "the author did not say" and "the author said they could not tell" are different facts.

assets.title: who-iris
assets.description: What is here, what is only referenced, and how to tell.

_folioMount_comment: F8/F9, bean jpjt. The reader's folio comes from cat-harness and must be the same folio in every library they browse — board-windows: "the test is not 'is this folio good' but 'is this the same folio'". These are the roots whose pages carry it; `check:folio-mount` fails the build for one that does not. uploads/ is EXEMPT with its reason, because it holds the captured IRIS source the replica is generated FROM, and rewriting a capture destroys the artefact ingestion exists to preserve.

exempt.reason: captured IRIS source — the artefact ingestion exists to preserve, not a page this repository authors

directories.description: The gettext side of who-iris's own strings, one directory per target locale: the `glossary/who-iris--who-terms` catalogues that translate this instance's WHO terms. Moved here from cat-harness/translations/ on the owner's ruling of 2026-10-04, "move things to semantically appropriate place" (bean riit): a scheme's translations sit with the instance whose terms they translate.

The three IRIS items this instance holds rather than merely names: `wpr-rdo-2020-003-eng` (the WPRO publication style guide, and the worked example whose full DSpace item record drives the `iris-dspace` skill), `who-pub-tps-931` and `9789241548960-eng`. They are the `materialized` end of the catalogue -- every other node under `catalogue/nodes/` is `referenced`, and the three here are what a materialization actually looks like. `milnorlink` is NOT here and never was an IRIS item; it went to folio-assistant-sci (bean r1lz). The id is `library`, the CONVENTIONAL one, so this entry OVERRIDES the default rather than joining it: overrides match on id and never on path, so a distinct id at the same path yields two entries for one directory and every fan-out consumer scans it twice. Measured while doing exactly that.
directories._comment_corpusOnly: CORPUS ONLY since 2026-09-30 (bean 2b5s, the owner's 'site/ + publish covers'). This entry carried `instanceRoot: true` while the replica pages lived here, and a mount copies the whole directory whose index.html it finds -- so the 1,367 ingestion sidecars were published at /who-iris/ AND /library/who-iris/ as if they were pages. The replica moved to `site/`, which is now the instance root; this directory has no index.html and is mounted nowhere. The covers the replica shows stay here, where the catalogue's localPath names them (bean yl5w), and the mount publishes exactly the ones a page embeds.
directories._comment_kindRouteRedirect: /library/who-iris/ stayed a live URL while it was a verbatim mount, so it keeps answering: `mount-instance-docs.ts` writes it as a one-file redirect to this directory's library viewer, /cat-harness/library/who-iris/, rather than letting an old link 404.

directories.description: The IRIS REPLICA: the home page, the community list, and one page per collection and per item, themed as IRIS and generated from `catalogue/` by `scripts/gen-iris-pages.ts` (gated by `bun run iris:pages:check`). It is what `/who-iris/` serves. Moved out of `library/` on 2026-09-30 (bean 2b5s) so that the corpus and its rendering are separate directories: before, the mount copied the corpus along with the pages. A page shows an item's cover by referencing `../library/<slug>-cover.png`; the build publishes exactly the files a page embeds, beside the replica, and not the directory they sit in.
directories._graphKinds_comment: `docs`, the one renderable kind the harness owns, because the mount publishes only renderable directories' pages and the replica is a finished HTML rendering of this instance's catalogue -- `folio` is authored block content with viewers, LaTeX and QA badges, which this is not. It shares the kind with `docs/`, and `withRoutes` settles which answers where: this directory is the instance root and serves /who-iris/, and the kind route /docs/who-iris/ stays with the sibling that is not the root, so the replica is published once rather than twice.
directories._comment_instanceRoot: The themed replica is what /who-iris/ serves — the owner's ruling, 'who-iris themed at /who-iris/'. Moved here from the `library` entry with the pages (bean 2b5s).

directories.readOnlyBasis: Records of content materialized from IRIS. Editing one in place would change what this repository claims IRIS holds, with nothing saying so -- which is the case bean `10s1` exists for. To work on one, copy it out.
directories._coverage_comment: The KG view, NOT the replica. `library/community-list.html` and its collection/item pages answer "what does IRIS look like"; this answers "what does this catalogue know, and what does it record that it does not know". The difference is load-bearing here: who-iris/AGENTS.md says the gap between the modelled nodes and the million upstream files IS THE POINT rather than a backlog, and nothing rendered that until 2026-09-22 -- the one fact the instance is built around was the one fact no reader could see. It also surfaces the gate verdicts, where `copyright` and `restrictions` are `unknown` on every held bitstream: a question nobody has answered, which a page showing only "3 materialized" would have read as a clearance. HTML rather than markdown because who-iris declares no `composed` directory -- its docs are MOUNTED after Jekyll, so a .md here would be copied verbatim and never rendered.

visualiser._ref_comment: THE CONVENTIONAL PATH, not this instance's own tree. `harnessTiles` links a declared visualiser only when its ref is under the published site directory, because the published path is then the ref with that prefix stripped -- nothing to resolve, nothing to guess. This ref was `who-iris/docs/catalogue.html` until 2026-09-22: inside who-iris's own tree, which the build MOUNTS at /docs/who-iris/, so the strip could not compute it and no tile linked the page. Built, declared, resolving and unreachable -- bean `ha78`, issue #886. The page is generated by `gen-iris-pages.ts`, which composes this same route from `subjectPage` rather than spelling it, so the generator and the discovery cannot drift apart.
visualiser.title: Catalogue

directories.description: The catalogue itself: `catalogue.json` declares the corpus and its measured size; `nodes/` holds one `folio-catalogue-node/v1` per community, collection or item; `records/` holds the `folio-dublin-core/v1` metadata an item node points at through `metadataRef`. TWELVE nodes today — 9 referenced, 3 materialized, 0 unknown — against 1,057,223 files upstream, and that gap IS the point. `bun run check:catalogue` verifies every node validates and every metadataRef, libraryId and parent path resolves; a Zod schema can require the reference and structurally cannot check the file is there.

directories.readOnlyBasis: NOT frozen, and the exception is worth stating. This is the ingestion DROP ZONE -- `adapters/document/paths.ts` creates it on a first ingest precisely so somebody can put something in it. The bytes it holds are materialized; the directory is a write target, and those are different questions. Declaring it read-only because its contents are materialized would freeze the one place a person is supposed to write.
directories.description: The incoming queue — raw captures as dropped, before ingestion. NOT L1 and not greppable as corpus. Holds the IRIS capture for the worked example: the saved DSpace item page, its asset zip (which carries the IRIS web theme), the full item record in qualified Dublin Core, and the item page printed to PDF — the last recorded with role `none`, because 'we looked and it is not what it appears to be' is a different fact from 'nobody looked'.

coverage._visualiser_comment: SHARED WITH THE `library` ENTRY, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE — recorded 2026-09-23 (issue #1009) because it was not. The library viewer carries an uploads SECTION scoped to the same subject (`G.uploads.filter(inScope)` in `gen-library-viz.ts`), so one page answers both graphs for this instance and there is no `uploads/who-iris/` page to point at. An unavoidable duplicate is fine; an UNCHECKED one is not, which is the rule the sibling `catalogue` entry's own ref comment exists to satisfy. The visible cost of the silence: the harness rail shows `library` and `uploads` as two entries resolving to one URL, and nothing said why. If an `uploads/<instance>/` viewer is ever generated for who-iris — `folio-assistant` already has one — this should point at it instead.

directories.description: Deliberately thin, per 'mionimal tools in who specific stuff'. ONE skill package: `iris-dspace`, how IRIS uses DSpace and qualified Dublin Core, with what a later tool needs stated as nine checkable requirements. The Dublin Core TYPE is generic and lives in folio-assist-core; enumeration and subsetting live in large-datasets; OCR stays a cat-harness platform tool. Since 2026-10-01 it also holds the WHO STYLE GUIDE's three house voices under `voices/`, declared from within by `skills.json` (bean `cmsl`) -- they were the separate staged instance `who-style-guide` until the owner's 2026-09-30 ruling, 'who voices style guide is derivative KG content from who-iris, merge content into subgraph. including docs.' (bean `qsx4`).
directories._tile_comment: Carried over from cat-harness's mirror of this directory, which placement PR0 (bean ejye) removed: the tile title is the owner's to state.

directories._comment: MOVED HERE from who-style-guide/glossary/ with the rest of the style guide (bean qsx4, owner 2026-09-30: 'who voices style guide is derivative KG content from who-iris, merge content into subgraph'). The id stays the CONVENTIONAL `glossary`, so this entry overrides the inherited default rather than adding a second entry at the same path. Bean ftu0 had put the glossary with the voices because it is a HOUSE rule about wording; the voices are now here, so it followed them, and the reason ftu0 gave still holds.
directories.description: The WHO glossary: folio-glossary/v1 schemes of terms the WHO publications use under more than one name -- a HOUSE rule about wording, like the style-guide voices under skills/voices/ (bean ftu0). An alternative label is recorded only where a publication STATES the equivalence, and each term cites that sentence in this instance's own library; a count or a latent-semantic cosine is never the evidence. The scheme's source is the who-guideline-development voice, so its terms are minted in this instance's namespace. Rendered on the glossary/ page and checked by check:glossary, both of which read every instance's declared glossary directory.

directories._comment: Themes this instance DERIVED from sources it holds, bean j66n. `iris-web` is read off the compiled stylesheet DSpace served with the captured item page; `who-wpro-publication` is read off the style guide's own pages 6, 7, 12, 14 and 18. Declared rather than left implicit because an undeclared directory is the dh4f defect -- every declaration-driven consumer scans nothing and reports a clean run over it, which is exactly what `docs/` did with 241 files until 2026-09-20. These are NOT the platform's twelve themes: those are cat-harness's own furniture, and a palette read off a WHO style guide is subject matter, which the root AGENTS.md keeps out of the platform.
directories._inheritance_comment: Not reproduced in a dependent folio, and no field here says so: `themes` is not a `perInstance` graph kind (graph-kind-registry.ts), so a downstream folio gets a themes/ directory only where it already has one and never an empty one. That is right for this entry -- it says where THIS instance's themes live, not a workspace every downstream folio needs. `uploads/` and `library/` differ because their kinds ARE `perInstance`: a dependent folio ingests its OWN sources into its own copies. Before 2026-09-30 this was the per-entry `dependents: skip`, retired by the owner (option A) because the same kind was declared both ways in different declarations.

directories._comment: The RENDERABLE surface of this instance -- the ingested-IRIS replica pages, generated from catalogue/ by scripts/gen-iris-pages.ts and gated by `bun run iris:pages:check`. Declared because the owner's URL contract (2026-09-20) makes it addressable: `<baseURL>/<instantiated-harness>/<path_to_rendered_content>`, so these land at `<baseurl>/who-iris/community-list`. Undeclared, it would be the dh4f defect on the one directory a READER actually reaches -- exactly what cat-harness/docs/ was until 2026-09-20 with 241 files. These are pages THIS instance publishes about its own catalogue. `docs` is a `perInstance` graph kind (graph-kind-registry.ts), so a dependent folio has its OWN docs/ for its own pages; it never inherits these files, which stay this instance's.
directories.description: The viewer for this instance's docs, BUILT BY cat-harness — the owner's rule that a harness which instantiates a directory makes a visualiser for it. Declared HERE, in this instance's own file, rather than in the root's: `compose-docs.docsLayers` treats every docs-kind entry in `cat-harness.json` as a COMPOSITION LAYER, so declaring this directory there would overlay this instance's `index.md` onto the site's own. Measured — `compose-docs.test.ts` failed exactly that way when tried. The ref resolves because `injectRails` measures against the BUILT instance's docs prefix (cat-harness's), not the declaring instance's, which is the same reason `who-iris-library`'s cat-harness-built ref resolves today. This directory IS mounted verbatim at `/docs/who-iris/` as well, and the two are different things: the mount is a byte-for-byte copy of the directory, this is an index OF it. The rail links here, which is what `visualiserHref` exists to make happen.

The catalogue checker, the cover generator and `gen-iris-pages.ts` -- the instance-local generator `wjfu` cites as the precedent for every other one here (*"instance-local generator, static HTML, committed, gated"*). Cited as a model by another instance's bean while being undeclared itself, which is the sharpest form of the `ylj7` defect: a directory can be the corpus's own worked example and still be invisible to every consumer that walks declarations.

Source descriptors (`folio-source-descriptor/v1`): how to ENUMERATE WHO IRIS and ask it for a SUBSET, so an agent asked for part of it is not told the API by a human every time. Moved here from large-datasets' `sources/` on 2026-10-01 (owner ruling: large-datasets dissolves into cat-harness; bean `j7ql`), because a descriptor is ABOUT one corpus and the instance that holds or catalogues that corpus owns it — the schema stays in cat-harness. Its far-apart sibling, Lean mathlib, is in folio-assistant-sci: IRIS items stand alone (`subsetIsSelfContained: true`), three identifier systems, paged REST.

The GENERATED prefix-sharded identifier lookup over this catalogue's REFERENCED nodes: `manifest.json` plus JSON shards keyed by id prefix, each under 64 KiB. Written by `cat-harness-tools/scripts/gen-id-lookup.ts` (`bun run id-lookup`, gated by `id-lookup:check`), which finds this directory by its id `id-lookup` and never by this instance's name; read by `cat-harness-tools/id-lookup/lookup.js`. Here rather than beside the generator because an instance hosts its own generated outputs (D3, bean `j7ql`, 2026-10-01). Edit the catalogue, never the shards: the generator replaces this directory whole.

What auditing THIS instance produced, committed so a consumer can tell "never audited" from "audited clean" — a printed verdict cannot, which is why every QA verdict here is a sidecar. TWO kinds live here and the files declare which they are via $schema: kg-qa/v1, one per audited subject, in a tree mirroring the subject’s own path, and ONE kg-qa-manifest/v1 recording the auditor’s identity for all of them. The manifest moved here from skills/ on 2026-09-27: kg-audit.ts writes it unconditionally, so its old home created a skills/ directory holding no skills in every instance that has none. At declaration time that is 2 files across scenarios (1), skills (1). No qa-results/v1 and no witnesses: this instance runs no document build and no witness-producing computation, and declaring kinds it does not hold would be an over-claim. `qa` is a `perInstance` graph kind (graph-kind-registry.ts), because a dependent audits its OWN graph — these verdicts are about this instance’s nodes, and inheriting them would attribute one instance’s findings to another. Declared WITH its files in one commit, per bean dh4f: a declared-but-absent directory makes a consumer scan nothing and report a clean run over it.

stickies._comment: WHO-IRIS'S OWN CARD, bean v8n5. The owner ruled that each initiated harness contributes its own initialization card, and a theme is reached THROUGH a sticky -- so this card is also what gives the who-iris board tile and navbar entry their theme. It cites `iris-sticky` BY REFERENCE, owner first (`themeByRef`): a sticky-kind theme declared in this instance's own `themes/`, DERIVED from `iris-web` (inherits its palette), which was measured from the captured DSpace stylesheet. The platform holds no WHO colour; `gen-themes-css.ts` finds the theme by this instance's declaration and emits its CSS at build time. `bodyFrom: description` so the words are read from this declaration's own `description` and cannot drift from it.

_icon_comment: THE INSTANCE'S MARK, copied OUT of uploads/ rather than referenced there. `10s1`: a materialised copy of somebody else's artefact is read-only and the copy-out is step one — so `docs/assets/img/who-emblem.svg` is this instance's own asset, and the capture under `uploads/wpr-rdo-2020-003-eng/iris-capture/` stays untouched as the record of what was ingested. OWNER'S CHOICE, 2026-09-22, made against a stated alternative: this is the WHO emblem and wordmark, NOT the blue `iris.` wordmark the IRIS repository uses as its own brand. Swapping it is one `src` and one re-measured `avatarRegion`.

images.title: WHO emblem
images.description: The World Health Organization emblem — the rod of Asclepius over a globe in an olive-branch wreath — beside the words World Health Organization, in the organisation's blue (#0093D5). 580.8x178 as authored; declared 581x178 because the schema takes integers and the 0.2px is below anything the squareness check resolves.

_icon_restored_comment: RESTORED 2026-10-04 (bean `2vpn`). Owner, 2026-09-23: *"no logo on who-iris icon (for now). just WHO blue"* removed this pointer; on 2026-10-04, asked what who-iris's top navbar mark should be after it showed the letter "W" on every page, the owner chose BOTH the one-resolver fix and *"restore WHO emblem"*. So `icon` points at the emblem again, cropped by its declared `avatarRegion`, and the `who-iris` entry in `schemas/avatars.ts` (the open book in WHO blue, hue 199) stays as the mark's FALLBACK — `harness-tiles.ts` resolves a theme card avatar first (who-iris has none: IRIS imagery is somebody else's artefact), then this icon, then that glyph.
